papers.title: Psychological Inflexibility and Attitudes Toward Violence in Close Relationships: Associations With Emotion Regulation Difficulties and Self-Compassion.
papers.abstract: Attitudes toward violence constitute a significant dimension of problems experienced in close relationships. Individuals' psychological inflexibility, together with variables such as emotion regulation and self-compassion, has been associated with attitudes toward violence in close relationships. The present cross-sectional study aims to examine the indirect associations involving difficulties in emotion regulation and self-compassion in the relationship between psychological inflexibility and attitudes toward violence in close relationships. The sample of the study consisted of 253 Turkish volunteers (217 females [85.8%] and 36 males [14.2%]). Participants' ages ranged from 18 to 35, with a mean age of 27.89 (SD = 4.97). The analyses were conducted using two-stage structural equation modeling. The indirect associations among the study variables were examined using the bootstrapping method following the structural equation modeling analyses. The findings revealed statistically significant indirect associations involving difficulties in emotion regulation and self-compassion in the relationship between psychological inflexibility and attitudes toward violence in close relationships. In conclusion, the findings suggest that psychological inflexibility, difficulties in emotion regulation, and self-compassion are meaningfully associated with attitudes toward violence in close relationships. These findings contribute to the understanding of attitudes toward violence in intimate relationships.

papers.title: When Men Are Victims: A Review and Theoretical Explanations of Childhood Sexual Abuse and Later Adult Sexual Violence Revictimization and Perpetration Among Men Who Have Sex with Men.
papers.abstract: Childhood sexual abuse (CSA) is disproportionally reported by men who have sex with men (MSM), yet its association with sexual violence in adulthood remains understudied. This narrative review synthesizes research on CSA and later adult sexual revictimization and adult sexual violence perpetration among MSM, drawing on gender-role socialization and minority stress theory to contextualize the findings. Searches of Google Scholar, PubMed, and PsycINFO identified 11 primary studies (10 on revictimization and one on perpetration) and two contextual reviews. Most included studies used U.S.-based samples. Across studies, CSA was associated with adult sexual revictimization within and outside intimate relationships, with some evidence that greater frequency or severity of childhood abuse was associated with later victimization. Revictimization was also linked with psychological distress, substance use, and sexual health concerns. In contrast, the evidence on CSA and adult sexual violence perpetration among MSM was too limited to support firm conclusions or assumptions of a victim-to-perpetrator cycle. Gender-role socialization highlights barriers to disclosure and help-seeking, while minority stress theory situates survivors' experiences with stigma, discrimination, and unequal access to support. Inconsistent definitions and predominantly cross-sectional studies limit interpretation. Future longitudinal research should distinguish sexual identity from behavior and examine how gendered and structural conditions shape victimization across the life course.

papers.title: Extrahepatic malignancies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: from epidemiologic association to risk prediction and screening.
papers.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with an increased risk of extrahepatic malignancies, although these associations vary across cancer sites and populations. Given the high prevalence of MASLD and its close relationship with established cancer risk factors, epidemiological associations alone are insufficient to inform screening decisions. The key clinical question is whether information obtained during routine MASLD assessment can improve cancer-specific risk prediction to guide clinical management. In this Review, we examine the evidence for risk stratification beyond established cancer risk factors, focusing on fibrosis severity, metabolic phenotype, genetic susceptibility, and routinely available non-invasive tests. Although the fibrosis-4 index and selected MASLD phenotypes have been associated with incident malignancy, most studies rely on composite cancer outcomes, with limited evidence for site-specific discrimination, calibration, incremental predictive value, or external validation. Associations between liver stiffness and extrahepatic cancer have also been inconsistent, leaving the independent contribution of fibrosis severity to extrahepatic cancer risk uncertain. No MASLD-related measure provides validated cancer-specific absolute-risk estimates sufficient to justify modifying established screening strategies. Colorectal cancer represents a promising setting for evaluating risk-adapted approaches. Future research should prioritize cancer-specific prediction models, establish clinically actionable absolute-risk thresholds, and determine whether incorporating MASLD-related measures into screening decisions improves clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Evaluating pair-bonding and social relationship strength across social contexts in prairie voles (Microtus ochrogaster).
papers.abstract: Social relationships play a critical role in modulating stress responses, adjusting behavior, and regulating physiology. Changes in the social environment, including cohabitation and partner status, can shape behavioral and physiological outcomes, yet the extent of influence to physiological changes remains unclear. In this study, we characterized the complexity of relationships in the prairie vole (Microtus ochrogaster) across four different social contexts, including: isolated voles, females paired with vasectomized males, females paired with intact males, and same-sex sibling pairs. We investigated the establishment and development of these varied social relationships through the use of four behavioral testing paradigms. In the partner preference test, we found that subjects in all social groups preferred spending time with their partner rather than a stranger. In a separation distress paradigm, subjects spent more time in the nest when their partners were present than when alone, whereas grooming increased during isolation. During social buffering, affiliative behaviors were elevated in the presence of a partner. In the homecage, sibling subjects spent more time huddling, and lunging was elevated in vasectomized breeders compared to intact breeders, suggesting differences in baseline social dynamics with the presence of pups. We used these behavioral measures to identify two sets of factors that describe relationship quality. Together, the findings underscore that social relationships are not a unified construct, but reflect multiple complex responses. This study highlights the importance of characterizing complex social behavior across different relationship types.

papers.title: Unlocking the unparalleled paleoclimate record of Antarctic blue ice areas.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Ice uniquely provides direct samples of ancient atmosphere, enabling measurements of greenhouse gases contemporaneous to temperature reconstructions. Blue ice areas (covering 1% of the surface of Antarctica) hold a largely underexplored paleoclimate record that can extend beyond deep ice cores (that is, older than 1.5 My), covering periods in which global surface temperatures were similar to projected future temperatures. Blue ice areas expose ancient ice directly at the surface or at shallow depths due to net ablation and redirected ice flow, providing access to old ice at logistically reduced costs. However, the analysis and interpretation of blue ice samples is challenging, given the complex flow patterns in these regions that result in tilted layers, inversions and discontinuities in the stratigraphy, and complex ice-bedrock interactions. This paper presents a succinct review of state-of-the-art blue ice research, placed in the context of established ice core research, and argues that to advance the search for ancient ice, efforts in blue ice areas should focus on: i) collecting dated surface samples, ii) investigating the relationship between the age of the ice and other datable evidence, such as moraines, dust layers, meteorites, and exposed bedrock, and iii) developing models that can capture the typically disturbed or discontinuous stratigraphy. Together with advances in analytical techniques that address, for example, contamination and absolute dating, these efforts could lead to the recovery of the oldest ice on Earth, unravel warm climates of the past, and improve future climate change projections.

papers.title: Protocol to identify and date ancient whole-genome duplications using KS age distributions and molecular clock estimates.
papers.abstract: Ancient polyploidy, the result of whole-genome duplication (WGD), has occurred repeatedly throughout the tree of life, yet the inference of ancient WGDs remains a challenging task. Here, we present a computational protocol for the inference of ancient WGDs using KS age distributions and molecular clock estimates. We describe steps to search for the remnants of ancient WGDs and the ensuing identification and dating in an evolutionary time frame. This protocol is suitable for WGD investigation of newly generated genome data. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Chen et al.1.

papers.title: Three novel Pseudanabaena species (Pseudanabaenales, Cyanobacteriophyta) from frozen glacial and post-glacial lakes in polar regions: Cryotolerance as a potential mechanism for long-term survival of freeze-thaw adapted types.
papers.abstract: Frozen Pseudanabaena-dominated phytobenthic mats were collected from four ecologically similar, shallow, low-conductivity glacial and post-glacial early Holocene lakes in the Arctic and Antarctica. Four isolated strains were subsequently analyzed using a polyphasic approach (morphology, ultrastructure, 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, ITS rRNA region analyses), resulting in the description of three novel Pseudanabaena species (P. gelidogaleata, P. lacugelata, and P. prelichiana). Field observations, complemented with controlled in vitro experiments, confirmed the ability of the new species to withstand freeze-thaw treatments, irrespective of the cryogenic intensity (-20, -80, -196°C). Despite their similar cryoresistance, all species displayed unique phenotypic features-such as cell-shape plasticity with polymorphic "behavior" (within-trichome transitions in morphology), variable constrictions across a range of intensities (including some rare constriction patterns), and different types of swollen/involution cells. These findings, along with ultrastructural observations, blur traditional taxonomic boundaries between Pseudanabaena and related genera. Molecular clock analyses confirmed four diversification lineages within Pseudanabaena and revealed that the three new species represent ancient lineages predating their current habitats, with evolutionary origins dating back to the Mesozoic and Eocene epochs. Overall, the results propose a potential mechanism of long-term survival of Pseudanabaena, probably facilitated by cryopreservation within frozen lakes. Comprehensive molecular analyses strongly suggested a common ancestor between the Arctic P. gelidogaleata and several psychrotolerant strains isolated from Antarctica. This finding may further support the hypothesis of a more global distribution of cold-adapted ecotypes. The study provides new insights into the complex ecology, biogeography, and adaptability of Pseudanabaena cryotypes under extreme conditions.

papers.title: Midwife-Performed Point-of-Care Ultrasounds in a Community Birth Center Setting: A Program Evaluation.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Midwife Center for Birth and Women's Health is an accredited, freestanding community birth center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Prior to 2023, prenatal ultrasound services were not available on site, requiring referral to outside facilities and potentially disrupting continuity of care. In the fall of 2023, certified midwives implemented a point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) program offering first-trimester dating, third-trimester fetal presentation evaluation, and modified biophysical profiles. This program evaluation examined clinical outcomes, client and midwife satisfaction, and financial impact following implementation. METHODS: Staff certified nurse-midwives completed a 2-day ultrasound training and began performing limited prenatal ultrasounds. A retrospective chart review was conducted for clients receiving ultrasounds between February 15, 2024, and January 7, 2025. Clinical outcomes, including birth location, gestational age, and mode of birth, were reviewed. Satisfaction surveys were distributed via email to clients and midwives. A cost analysis compared reimbursement and revenue with program expenses. RESULTS: During the evaluation period, 407 ultrasounds were performed for 279 clients, generating $39,144 in revenue. Dating ultrasound accuracy was comparable to outside facilities, with similar rates of estimated due date revision. Malpresentation was identified in 9 clients at 36 weeks, facilitating a timely referral for external cephalic version. Most births occurred at term, with only 2 preterm births and no adverse outcomes attributable to POCUS. Satisfaction survey responses demonstrated high client and midwife satisfaction. Responses to the midwife survey suggested an interest in additional ultrasound training. DISCUSSION: Midwife-performed POCUS was safely integrated into an accredited, freestanding community birth center, supporting continuity of care, clinical decision-making, and financial sustainability without negatively impacting

papers.title: Romantic Attachment and Sexual Dissatisfaction Among Spanish-Speaking Couples: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Emotionally Focused Couple Therapy.
papers.abstract: This study examined whether emotionally focused couple therapy (EFCT) reduces sexual dissatisfaction and whether romantic attachment insecurity is associated with sexual dissatisfaction among Spanish-speaking couples experiencing relationship distress. Seventy heterosexual couples from Argentina, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Mexico, and Spain were randomly assigned to EFCT (8-20 sessions) or to a wait-list control condition. Participants completed repeated assessments of sexual dissatisfaction (MSI-R SEX subscale) and romantic attachment insecurity (ECR-36). Longitudinal mixed-effects models and an actor-partner interdependence model were used to evaluate trajectories of change and dyadic interdependence. EFCT was associated with a small but statistically significant overall reduction in sexual dissatisfaction. The treatment effect did not differ significantly by sex, and exploratory sex-stratified results should be interpreted with caution. Greater romantic attachment anxiety and avoidance were associated with higher sexual dissatisfaction, both as stable between-person differences and as session-to-session within-person fluctuations. Concurrent actor-partner interdependence models (APIM) analyses indicated that both actor attachment anxiety and avoidance were associated with greater sexual dissatisfaction, whereas partner attachment anxiety and avoidance were not significantly associated with actor sexual dissatisfaction. Findings highlight the relevance of attachment-related processes for understanding sexual dissatisfaction and suggest that integrating EFCT with interventions more directly targeting sexual functioning and communication may further enhance treatment outcomes.

papers.title: Hydroxyl-Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One-Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation.
papers.abstract: One-step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl-orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone-carbonyl pocket-site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs+, Sr2+ and UO2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl-orchestrated enol-imine to keto-enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone-carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO22+ uptake of 336 mg g-1 and a Cs+ permeation flux of 0.26 mol m-2 h-1, while exhibiting suppressed Sr2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs+/Sr2+ and Cs+/UO2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl-orchestrated crystallization and pocket-site engineering as a powerful approach for multi-component ion separations.

papers.title: Steering atomic hydrogen production at zero-valent iron-water interface via proton-coupled electron accumulation for efficient dechlorination.
papers.abstract: Ambient hydrogenation induced by atomic hydrogen (*H) in the zero-valent iron (Fe0)-water system holds great promise for deep dechlorination of refractory chlorinated organic compounds (COCs), yet sluggish proton transfer and mismatched electron delivery at the interface limit efficient *H supply for hydrodechlorination. Inspired by bifunctional metalloenzymes, bismuth/nitrogen co-modified Fe0 (4Bi-1N-Fe0) was designed to simultaneously gather protons and electrons at the Fe0-water interface via coupled accumulation, steering *H generation toward targeted dechlorination. N sites strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, enabling relay proton accumulation, stabilizing *H, and enhancing dechlorination selectivity. Meanwhile, Bi sites construct fast interfacial charge-transfer channels and optimize Fe electronic structures via p-d orbital hybridization, enhancing electron density and surface *H binding. Driven by Bi-N cooperativity, 4Bi-1N-Fe0 delivers a dechlorination rate of 2.69 h-1 (trichloroethylene, TCE), which is 59.8 and 268.9 times that of singly modified Bi-Fe0 and N-Fe0, respectively. Furthermore, 4Bi-1N-Fe0 exhibits broad-spectrum dechlorination (for 4-CP, 2,4-DCP, FF, and CAP), remarkable 150-day stability, and low ecological risk, as confirmed by unimpaired survival of E. coli and unaffected germination and growth of rice and wheat upon leachate exposure. This strategy resolves the trade-off between sluggish *H generation and rapid *H loss, providing a new avenue for remediating COC-contaminated wastewater.

papers.title: Safe and inclusive spaces in co-produced research: co-creating a practical guide.
papers.abstract: Co-produced research requires meaningful collaboration amongst Indigenous people, patients/people with lived and living experience, researchers, and others who ultimately use research knowledge. Despite good intentions, traditional academic environments, structures, and hierarchies where research is done can create unintentional barriers and make meaningful collaboration among partners difficult. Few resources integrate trauma-informed care; Indigenous ways of knowing, being and doing; and, anti-oppression frameworks specifically for the practical demands of co-produced, patient- and community-engaged health research meetings and events. To address this gap, the Brain-Heart Interconnectome co-produced a practical, living resource called Tips to Create Safe Spaces. Drawing from trauma-informed care; patient engagement principles; Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and doing; and anti-oppression frameworks, our team collaboratively developed actionable guidance organized across three stages of research meetings and events: planning, conducting, and debriefing. The resulting guidance emphasizes important practices such as proactively offering accommodations (rather than placing the burden on individuals to request them), using facilitation practices that dismantle hierarchies to create multiple pathways for participation, co-designing meetings and materials with partners from the outset, and collecting feedback in ways that are safe and that demonstrably inform future practices. Creating safe spaces is an ongoing process that requires humility and sustained commitment. Research teams are encouraged to adopt and adapt this guidance, commit to ongoing learning, and treat the creation of safe spaces as a ongoing practice rather than a one-time effort. When all team members feel genuinely supported and valued, co-produced research becomes more rigorous, relevant, and capable of driving meaningful change. papers.title: Preventing congenital syphilis: a review of maternal screening.
papers.abstract: Congenital syphilis remains one of the most preventable causes of stillbirth, neonatal mortality, and infant morbidity worldwide. Despite inexpensive diagnostic tests and effective treatment, surveillance indicates a resurgence of maternal and congenital syphilis. Untreated maternal infection can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal death, or severe congenital disease. In 2022, the World Health Organization estimated 700,000 congenital syphilis cases worldwide, resulting in nearly 390,000 adverse pregnancy outcomes, including fetal and neonatal deaths and infants born with clinical disease. Implementation failures across the prevention cascade continue to undermine global elimination efforts. Surveillance data demonstrate concerning increases in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and Australia, while substantial disparities persist among Indigenous and marginalised populations. Congenital syphilis prevention relies on timely antenatal screening, early diagnosis, and prompt treatment with benzathine penicillin. However, prevention failures, including limited access to antenatal care, missed screening opportunities, delayed treatment, and inadequate partner management, continue to drive transmission despite the availability of diagnostics and treatment. The COVID-19 pandemic further exposed vulnerabilities in maternal health services, widening existing prevention gaps and weakening surveillance systems. Conversely, successful elimination initiatives demonstrate that congenital syphilis is preventable when screening, treatment, surveillance, and health-system implementation are effectively integrated. Strengthening antenatal screening programmes, expanding access to rapid point-of-care diagnostics, implementing repeat screening where appropriate, and reinforcing integrated surveillance systems should therefore remain global priorities. Ultimately, eliminating congenital syphilis is not a technological but an implementation c

papers.title: Evidence translation and community engagement within US cancer centers.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The National Cancer Institute requires cancer centers to maintain Community Outreach and Engagement components (COEs) that bridge research and community priorities to support evidence translation. Limited information exists on how COEs implement evidence-based interventions (EBIs) with community partners. We describe how COEs translate evidence into practice and promising community engagement practices. METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews in 2021 with COE leaders at 38 NCI-designated US cancer centers. EBIs were categorized along a community engagement continuum, and cross-cutting themes and highly-engaged practices were identified. Transcripts were double-coded and analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. RESULTS: COEs implemented a wide range of EBIs at varying levels of community engagement. Implementation was shaped by community- and data-driven priority setting, leadership support, staffing constraints, and sustainability challenges. Highly-engaged EBIs involved community partners in identification, adapting materials, training faculty/staff on community engagement, and participating in evaluation and data analysis. They were most common among COEs with strong leadership support and dedicated funding. CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest well-supported COEs enabled more highly engaged EBI implementation. Institutional commitment and meaningful community partnership roles are important considerations for COEs seeking to embed community engagement throughout implementation and enhance reach and effectiveness of EBIs to reduce cancer disparities.

papers.title: The computational genesis of a self: Representational time and self-modeling in living systems.
papers.abstract: The transition from inanimate physicochemical dynamics to autonomous agency represents a fundamental challenge across theoretical biology and cognitive science. While traditional accounts have approached this transition through descriptive frameworks of autopoiesis, anticipatory systems, or the free energy principle, a formal deductive derivation linking computational irreducibility to functional agency has remained elusive. Here, a deductive framework demonstrates that core attributes of biological agency, specifically representational time, forward predictive processing, and self-modeling, emerge as operational necessities for an autonomous agent persisting within a computationally irreducible environment under a defined operational regime of delayed hazards and counterfactual pre-commitment. Grounded in organizational closure and viability theory, this framework establishes three principal deductive results. First, it is demonstrated that purely reactive behavioral strategies fail under observationally aliased environmental states requiring mutually incompatible viability-preserving actions; persisting under delayed viability hazards without lethal trial-and-error mandates the internal synthesis of a tripartite representational time. Second, this representational time is shown to share the operational organization of counterfactual forward prediction. Third, drawing upon closed-loop regulator theory, the Conant-Ashby theorem, and the internal model principle, it is established that evaluating candidate interventions over extended horizons (H > 1) in a coupled system requires internalizing the agent's own generative action dynamics, yielding a functional self-model distinct from simple state-dependent regulation. papers.title: Intimate Partner Violence Transition Patterns and Maternal Depression During Early Parenthood: A Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) poses substantial risks to maternal mental health. While IPV is a known risk factor for maternal depression, prior research often overlooks its heterogeneity. We applied latent transition analysis (LTA) to identify latent IPV transition patterns during early parenthood and examine their longitudinal associations with maternal depression at child age-5. We used data from the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study (N = 2,795), collected in 20 U.S. cities between 1999 and 2006. LTA identified IPV statuses across five domains (physical, sexual, emotional, economic, social isolation) at child age-1, age-3, and age-5. Bivariate analyses were performed to assess differences in baseline maternal demographic characteristics among the transition patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations between IPV transition patterns and maternal depression at child age-5, adjusting for baseline demographic characteristics. Four latent IPV statuses were identified: low-risk, emotional abuse, psychological abuse, and poly-victimization. Based on IPV transition probabilities, eight transition patterns were derived: consistent low-risk; consistent emotional abuse; consistent psychological abuse; consistent poly-victimization; escalating IPV; de-escalating IPV; poly-fluctuating; non-poly-fluctuating. Mothers with consistent and escalating IPV transition patterns experienced greater socioeconomic disadvantage, including lower educational attainment and higher prevalence of material hardship (p < .01). Patterns involving consistent or escalating IPV were significantly associated with maternal depression, with the highest odds observed with consistent poly-victimization (adjusted odds ratio = 7.56, 95% confidence interval [3.79, 15.10]). papers.title: Examining the Relation Between State-Level Economic Support Policies and Child Maltreatment and Intimate Partner Violence: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Each year, more than half a million children in the United States experience child maltreatment (CM), which impacts their physical, mental, and cognitive health. Intimate partner violence (IPV) often co-occurs in households where CM is experienced, and a growing body of evidence connects financial security to lower rates of both. OBJECTIVE: We examined the extent to which state-level economic support policies prevent CM and IPV. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: This review included studies that examined the impact of state economic support policies on children and youth (age birth to 18) and adult partners (18 and older) living in the United States. METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of studies published between 1990 and 2025 and included 37 studies. RESULTS: Generous, accessible economic support policies are associated with reductions in CM, reinforcing the protective role of economic security in child wellbeing. Findings associated with IPV were more nuanced: affordable housing is consistently associated with lower IPV but the impact of EITC, SNAP and minimum wage were inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: Research should examine the mechanisms driving changes in CM and IPV to clarify how and for whom these policies are most effective.
